evidence: run_mutant calls parse_expected_failing_test(spec), refuses ExpectedFailureError, preserves the parsed expectation in MutantResult, and passes it to classify_mutant_run after executing the mutation command.

classify_mutant_run invokes named_failure_refusal(reporter, output, expected_failing_test) inside the failed-test kill branch; only a None refusal produces KILLED, while a missing or unrelated named failure produces REFUSED.

mutation_expected_failure.py defines strict plan parsing and exact, case-sensitive matching against reporter-owned failed-test names; reporters without name support and unreadable runs explicitly refuse.
NodeTestReporter.failed_tests derives names only from the structurally selected TAP run and its owned in-sequence `not ok` results, avoiding whole-transcript matching.
Standing tests directly cover expected-name KILLED, unrelated-name REFUSED, and green-run SURVIVED semantics.

test_a_node_sweep_kills_only_the_expected_named_test runs mutate_and_restore end to end with real `node --test`, proving the declared failing name kills, an absent name refuses the same red run, and the mutated file is restored.
test_a_node_repository_gets_a_real_verdict and test_a_module_breaking_mutant_is_refused_not_killed additionally map real Node execution to genuine-kill and blocking-signal refusal behavior.

The test asserting that a failure elsewhere refuses explicitly identifies this behavior as the downstream blocking-signal claim, tying the repair to the uncovered-mutant class rather than merely testing helper parsing.
target_observations.summary: The current-main contents integrate the named-failure contract into mutation execution and kill classification, and provide standing recurrence tests for killed, refused, and survived outcomes, including end-to-end execution through a real Node test runner. This repairs the uncovered-mutant blocking-signal class by refusing a red run unless the declared test is among the reporter-owned failures.
